challenge.method: Checked the identifier and title inside the JSON, both publisher links and their recorded match values, the wording-change comments, and the generated representations against the publisher’s named notices and disclaimer.
challenge.results: SPDX records https://www.isc.org/licenses/ at order 0 and the older /downloads/software-support-policy/isc-license/ URL at order 1. Both are marked valid and live at 2026-09-16T17:05:17Z, both carry the string match value “false,” and both appear in seeAlso. SPDX reports a July 2007 change from “and” to “and/or.” Its template makes “/or” optional for matching. The generic year and owner and “THE AUTHOR” differ from the publisher’s named notices and “ISC.” Those differences defeat byte identity. Neither the link nor the matching rule establishes legal equivalence across wordings or licenses a particular copy of software.

limitations: The source URL pins the commit. The detail JSON contains no release-tag field, so the 3.29.0 label relies on the supplied release-to-revision mapping.
The link timestamps describe SPDX’s recorded observations. Link order supplies no redirect history or date when one publisher URL replaced another.
SPDX’s generated text, matching template, and HTML each have a separate representation scope. The crosswalk establishes neither reuse rights in those artifacts nor an applicable grant for any code.
